pages.title: An Anchor That Always Comes Back
pages.text: Minamitsu's anchor is a diamond pickaxe that can also be thrown. Hold the selection key to open its mode wheel (X by default): the mode decides what a throw does, and the hotbar icon shows it. Only the two storm throws cost spiritual power.

$(bold)Destroy$()$(br)Left click mines and attacks as usual. Right click throws the anchor: a block breaks in a 3×3×3 cube around the impact, a creature takes the hit, and the anchor flies back to your hand.$(br2)$(bold)Voyage$()$(br)An empty left click grabs a creature and drags it to you. Right click throws the anchor into a wall: if it hits a block it stays stuck there, pulls you over and holds you; right click to retrieve it, or sneak to let go. A throw that hits nothing pulls you from its furthest point and then returns.

$(bold)Storm$()$(br)Left click throws one anchor that deals area damage on impact. Right click is a charge: hold it for one second, then release to throw five anchors in a fan, each reaching 48 blocks. The two throws cost 5 and 10 spiritual power.$(br2)$(bold)Wet storms$()$(br)While a storm anchor is wet — in water, in rain or in a bubble column — it sheds danmaku along its flight and bursts into a spray of danmaku when it lands.

$(bold)One anchor at a time$()$(br)While the anchor is out, the hand looks empty and refuses another throw. A stuck Voyage anchor waits for you: right click within 3 blocks to call it home, or from farther away to be pulled in again.$(br2)$(bold)The power pool$()$(br)A Jizo will trade one experience level for spiritual power stored in the anchor. Without it the storm throws refuse to fire.
